title: Active concatenation preserves relative operadic cocartesian arrows
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations and edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and symmetric infinity-operads, their inert edges and active pointed maps as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. Use symmetric monoidal infinity categories in the sense of [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification]: cocartesian fibrations over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ whose fibers over $\langle n\rangle$ are the $n$-fold products of their color fiber under the inert projections, including the terminal zero fiber. For a symmetric infinity-operad $\mathcal C^\otimes$, write $\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ for its wide subcategory of active arrows. It has a canonical coherent symmetric monoidal operation $\oplus$ whose value on objects is concatenation of their finite tuples of colors, with the empty tuple as unit. For a map $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ of symmetric infinity-operads, the induced functor $q_{\mathrm{act}}$ preserves this concatenation, including its associativity, symmetry and unit coherences. If $q$ is also a cocartesian fibration, and $e_i:x_i\to y_i$ are finitely many active $q$-cocartesian edges, then $\bigoplus_i e_i:\bigoplus_i x_i\to\bigoplus_i y_i$ is $q$-cocartesian. In particular, if $e$ is active and $q$-cocartesian and $Z\in\mathcal E^\otimes$, then $e\oplus1_Z$ and $1_Z\oplus e$ are $q$-cocartesian. The assertions include the empty tuple and nullary active arrows.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.4.5, Remarks 2.2.4.6 and 2.2.4.8, printed pp. 212-213: active concatenation and stability of active cocartesian arrows. September 18, 2017 edition inspected online; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic assertion.

proof.text: Put $S=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and write $p_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C^\otimes\to S$ for its operadic projection. The active maps form a subcategory of $\mathsf{Fin}_*$, so restriction to them is a quasicategory: an inner-horn filler in $\mathcal C^\otimes$ lies over a chain of active maps, and its missing composite is active. Apply [lem-coef-active-operad-envelope-cocartesian] to $p_{\mathcal C}$, taking $\mathcal O^\otimes=S$ (the commutative operad). Its equivalence-lifting hypothesis holds: base equivalences are permutations, hence inert; their operadic cocartesian lifts are equivalences. Indeed [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] makes precomposition by such a lift an equivalence on every target mapping space, since its base is invertible; applying this to the source and target gives an inverse component and the two inverse equations. The inverse-component criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives an equivalence edge in the stated simplicial sense. The envelope $H_{\mathcal C}=\mathcal C^\otimes\times_S\operatorname{Act}(S)$ is therefore a cocartesian fibration over $S$ and an infinity-operad. Its operadic Segal fibers and [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification] make it a symmetric monoidal infinity category. In its fiber over $\langle1\rangle$, the active arrow out of $\langle n\rangle$ is the unique fold $\mu_n$; a morphism $c\to d$ lies in this fiber precisely when its pointed map $h$ satisfies $\mu_m h=\mu_n$, which says $h^{-1}(*)=\{*\}$. Thus this fiber is exactly $\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$, on all simplices, including $n=0$.

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Remark 2.2.4.3 and Corollary 2.2.4.5, printed pp. 211-212; Definition 2.1.1.10 and Lemma 2.2.4.15.

proof.text: For tuples $x$ of length $m$ and $y$ of length $n$, choose the tuple $z$ of their $m+n$ colors using the fiber Segal equivalence of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. Let $a:\langle m+n\rangle\to\langle2\rangle$ send the first block to $1$ and the second to $2$. The object $(z,a)$ of $H_{\mathcal C}$ has inert projections to $(x,\mu_m)$ and $(y,\mu_n)$: their source edges select the corresponding blocks. The envelope edge criterion makes these the cocartesian projections. Over the fold $\mu_2$, the square whose source edge is $1_z$ and whose target arrow is $\mu_{m+n}$ is again envelope-cocartesian, since $1_z$ is inert. Consequently the tensor in the active category sends $(x,y)$ to $z$, their concatenation. Every object of the envelope zero fiber has $a:\langle0\rangle\to\langle0\rangle$ and its source lies in the terminal-equivalent operadic zero fiber, so its unit transport gives the empty tuple, uniquely up to its coherent equivalence. The classification [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification] supplies the entire associativity, symmetry and unit coherence from the single cocartesian fibration, including empty blocks; no tensor operations or coherence maps are chosen independently. For an operad map $q$, the simplicial map $(c,a)\mapsto(qc,a)$ on these envelopes preserves cocartesian edges by the envelope criterion because $q$ preserves inert edges. The same classification makes it strong symmetric monoidal. Its color-fiber restriction is exactly $q_{\mathrm{act}}$, which proves coherent preservation of concatenation for every operad map, without assuming $q$ cocartesian.

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Lemma 2.2.4.15(4), Corollary 2.2.4.5 and Remark 2.2.4.6, printed pp. 211-212,216; explicit block-square computation.

proof.text: Now assume $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ cocartesian; put $p_E=p_Oq$ for their projections to $S$. We need two consequences of the mapping criterion. For an inert edge $v$ of $\mathcal E^\otimes$, both $v$ and $qv$ are cocartesian for $p_E$ and $p_O$, respectively, by the operad axioms and inert preservation in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]. For every target $z$, stack the precomposition mapping squares for $q$ and $p_O$. Their outer rectangle is the $p_E$ square. The bottom square and outer rectangle are homotopy pullbacks; cancellation in [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], applied after interchanging rows and columns, gives the top square as a homotopy pullback. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], $v$ is $q$-cocartesian. Conversely, if $v$ is $q$-cocartesian and $qv$ is inert, the two adjacent squares are homotopy pullbacks, so their outer rectangle is one. Thus $v$ is $p_E$-cocartesian over an inert pointed map, hence is inert. These arguments require only the inner fibrations $q,p_O,p_E$, all present here.

source.place: Remark 2.2.4.8, printed p. 212; expanded cocartesian assertions for the inert sides using the mapping-square test and pasting.

proof.text: Consider two active $q$-cocartesian arrows $e:x\to y$ and $f:z\to w$. Set $a=x\oplus z$, $b=y\oplus w$ and $g=e\oplus f$. Let $s_1:a\to x,s_2:a\to z$ and $t_1:b\to y,t_2:b\to w$ be the inert block projections from step 2. There are coherent squares $t_1g\simeq es_1$ and $t_2g\simeq fs_2$: in the envelope model these are the inert projections of the tuple of morphisms $(e,f)$. Both composites $es_1,fs_2$ are $q$-cocartesian by step 3 and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Choose a $q$-cocartesian lift $\gamma:a\to u$ of $qg$. The $K=\Delta^0$ fiber formula in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], with the mapping criterion identifying its convention, factors $g$ as $\delta\gamma$ for a vertical edge $\delta:u\to b$ over $1_{qb}$, with its specified triangle. Put $r_j=t_j\delta$. Then $r_1\gamma\simeq es_1$ and $r_2\gamma\simeq fs_2$. Cancellation in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] shows that $r_1,r_2$ are $q$-cocartesian. Since $qr_j=qt_j$ are inert, step 3 makes $r_j$ inert for $p_E$. The direction of each projection is from the concatenated object to a block; no inclusions into a concatenation are used.

source.place: Remark 2.2.4.8, printed p. 212: choose the lift gamma and construct its inert projections; expanded comparison triangle.

proof.text: Let $y,w$ have lengths $k,l$, so $u,b$ lie over $\langle k+l\rangle$. Compose the inert block projections $t_j,r_j$ of step 4 with the relevant inert color projection of $y$ or $w$. The composition assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes the resulting edges $R_i:u\to d_i$ and $T_i:b\to d_i$ $p_E$-cocartesian, where $d_i=y_i$ or $w_i$. They lie over the same inert color map $\rho_i$ and satisfy $T_i\delta\simeq R_i$. By the operad axioms in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], every source over the initial vertex of $\rho_i$ admits a $p_E$-cocartesian lift of $\rho_i$. The only other edges of $\Delta^1$ are identities, which have degenerate lifts by the composition-initiality node. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-base-restriction], with $h=\rho_i:\Delta^1\to S$, supplies a cocartesian fibration $E_i=\Delta^1\times_S\mathcal E^\otimes\to\Delta^1$ and says that $R_i,T_i$ remain cocartesian there. No global cocartesianness of $p_E$ is assumed.

source.place: Remark 2.2.4.8, printed p. 212: detect the vertical comparison under its inert color projections; nullary target case is the terminal zero fiber.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-transport-square] to $E_i\to\Delta^1$, the source edge $\delta:u\to b$, target edge $1_{d_i}$, and square $T_i\delta\simeq R_i$. For its transport $F_i$, it gives comparison equivalences $c_R:F_i(u)\to d_i$ and $c_T:F_i(b)\to d_i$ with $c_TF_i(\delta)\simeq c_R$. Hence $F_i(\delta)\simeq c_T^{-1}c_R$ is an equivalence. Indeed $c_R^{-1}c_T$ is its inverse by the associative and unital composition homotopies of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. These are exactly the inert color transports giving the fiber Segal equivalence in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction].

source.place: Remark 2.2.4.8, printed p. 212: detect the vertical comparison under its inert color projections; nullary target case is the terminal zero fiber.

proof.text: Under the fiber Segal equivalence of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], every component of $\delta$ is an equivalence by step 6. Taking their inverses and applying the quasi-inverse of the Segal equivalence gives an inverse for $\delta$ and its two inverse homotopies. If $k+l=0$, the fiber is equivalent to the terminal category, so its unique empty tuple of components gives the same conclusion. Finally precomposition by $\delta$ and its inverse gives homotopy-inverse maps on all target mapping spaces, by the associative and unital homotopies of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Thus the mapping square for $g=\delta\gamma$ is identified with the homotopy-pullback square for $\gamma$. The mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] makes $g=e\oplus f$ $q$-cocartesian.

source.place: Remark 2.2.4.8, printed p. 212: detect the vertical comparison under its inert color projections; nullary target case is the terminal zero fiber.

proof.text: Induct on the number of given edges. For zero edges the concatenated arrow is the identity of the empty tuple and is cocartesian by the degenerate-edge clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. For one edge it is the given edge. The induction step concatenates the first $r$ arrows, already active and cocartesian, with the next arrow and applies steps 4-7; a disjoint union of active pointed maps is active because no non-basepoint is sent to the basepoint. The associativity and permutation equivalences from step 2 identify all other parenthesizations and orders. Cocartesianness is unchanged by these equivalences: composing with their inverses identifies the mapping-square tests, using the associative and unital composition homotopies of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Identity arrows of any tuple $Z$ are active and cocartesian by the same degenerate-edge clause. Applying the binary case to $(e,1_Z)$ and $(1_Z,e)$ gives the two final assertions. Empty source blocks are allowed in all the finite pointed-set formulas, so nullary active arrows and the empty context have never been excluded.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q105-49acc2ab5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against HA (Sept 2017) Construction 2.2.4.1, Remark 2.2.4.3, Prop 2.2.4.4, Cor 2.2.4.5 and Remarks 2.2.4.6-2.2.4.8 (pp. 211-212), and HTT 2.4.1.3, 2.4.1.9, 2.4.1.12, 2.4.2.13 and 2.4.4.2, from the PDFs already fetched to /tmp. Item: the statement is unchanged and matches HA 2.2.4.5/2.2.4.8. Steps 1-4 and 8 are correct: the fiber identity mu_m h = mu_n iff h is active, the block concatenation, the inert/q-cocartesian equivalence by mapping-square pasting, the factorization g = delta gamma with r_j cancellation, and the finite induction including the empty and nullary cases. New step 5: R_i and T_i are p_E-cocartesian over the same rho_i, and the base-restriction hypotheses hold for h = rho_i: Delta^1 -> S (inert lifts plus degenerate lifts). New step 6: the transport square with x=u, y=b, x'=y'=d_i and v=1 gives F_i(delta) ~ c_T^-1 c_R, which is HA's componentwise-equivalence sentence. Step 7 is honestly elementary: the Segal equivalence reflects equivalences, the k+l=0 fiber is terminal, and the mapping criterion finishes. New node base-restriction is true: pullback of an inner fibration is inner, preservation is the dual of HTT 2.4.1.3(2), and reflection follows from the lift hypothesis as in HTT 2.4.1.12 and 2.4.2.13. New node transport-square is true: comparisons are equivalences by initiality, and naturality follows from the lambda-naturality and fiber formula of the transport node (HTT 2.4.4.2 dual). Both new nodes are statement-only, self-contained, strictly smaller than the item, and record leansearch, leanfinder and grep searches. A whole-DAG statement scan found no duplicates; nearest were categorical-base-change, left-cone-restriction, cartesian-fibration-pullback, local-transport-section-colimits and composition-initiality. No blueprint snapshot mentions cocartesian, so same_as=[] is right. All cited statements are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. There is no cycle, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and nothing cites SGA. Minor: the report mentions a citations.json that is not in the delivery; this is harmless. No fixes.
